theater: 四川成都府路至合州江防

battle.name: 蒙古攻四川之戰
battle.theater: 四川成都府路至合州江防
battle.brief: 寶祐四年（1256）夏，蒙古自雲南與甘肅兩路壓向四川，漢人降將劉整獻策，蒙古遂大舉南征；成都、嘉定、潼川諸城次第失守，宋軍退保合州釣魚城，憑山城扼江而守。卡面嘅配重投石車即宋元攻城序列中嘅長臂砲，以槓桿配重將石彈拋越城牆，與雲梯、穴地同施，卻難撼山城之險。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 一開始，這是蒙古帝國對南宋第一次成體系的正面進攻。蒙古方面，1251年即位的蒙哥汗把滅金、滅宋列為國策，先於1253年平定大理、取得雲南的馬匹與糧源，再於1256年下令南征：忽必烈領荊湖、襄樊方向的一路，自河套分兵入川者由蒙哥親率或遣重臣督之，東道自甘肅、洮州一線的兵歸紐璘、汪德臣節制，西道自雲南北上的兵由兀良合台與劉整等漢人將領帶路，軍隊另編「蒙古軍」與「漢軍」兩套：草原舊部居中，歸附的宋金降卒充攻城與後勤，攻城序列裡另有西域回回的砲手與工匠。編制上以十戶、百戶、千戶、萬戶為骨幹，攻城則臨時拼湊撞竿、雲梯與木料。宋方是四川一路的完整軍政建制：設四川制置司（後改安撫司、宣撫司）統成都府路、潼川府路、嘉定府路與川峽四路，1240年代餘玠入蜀後把制置司治所移往重慶，沿江築起合州釣魚城、嘉定大獲城、瀘州等山城作堡寨，屯兵屯糧；荊湖、兩淮、江西的援軍由賈似道在江漢一線策應，糧餉靠湖廣水運與四川井鹽、稻米接濟。雙方都明白，爭的不是一城一地，而是誰能先把川西平原與長江上游的補給線握在手裡。
countriesEn: At the outset this was the first systematic frontal offensive the Mongol Empire mounted against the Southern Song. On the Mongol side, Möngke Khan, who had taken the throne in 1251, made the destruction of Jin and Song a matter of state policy: he first reduced Dali in 1253 to gain the horses and the grain of Yunnan, and then ordered the southern campaign in 1256. Kublai led the line through Jinghu towards Xiangyang and Fancheng; the column that came into Sichuan from the Ordos side was led by Möngke in person or by great ministers he entrusted; the eastern line out of Gansu and Taozhou was under Nülin and Wang Dechen; and the troops coming north from Yunnan were guided by Han Chinese commanders such as Yuanliangtai and Liu Zheng. The host was organised in two systems, the Mongol troops and the Han troops, with the older steppe contingents in the middle and surrendered Song and Jin soldiers filling the assault and the service lines, while the besieging column also drew on Huihui trebuchet crews and craftsmen from the western regions. The backbone was the decimal organisation of ten, hundred, thousand and ten thousand households, and the siege equipment was improvised on the spot out of rams, ladders and timber. The Song side possessed the full military and administrative structure of the Sichuan circuit: a Directorate for Pacification of the Sichuan Circuits, later reorganised as the Anfu and Xuanfu offices, covering the Chengdu, Tongchuan and Jiading prefectural circuits together with the four circuits of the Sichuan gorges. After Yu Jie entered Sichuan in the 1240s he moved the seat of the directorate to Chongqing and raised hill forts along the river — Diaoyu at Hezhou, Dahuocheng at Jiading, the stronghold at Luzhou — where troops and grain were stockpiled. Reinforcements from Jinghu, Lianghuai and Jiangxi were directed by Jia Sidao on the Jianghan line, and the supply of the war came by water transport out of Huguang together with the salt wells and the rice of Sichuan. Both sides understood that the object was not any single city but the holding of the western Sichuan plain and of the supply line at the headwaters of the Yangtze.
people: 留下姓名的，蒙古一方比宋方多。宋方最關鍵的人物是餘玠：他在四川的十來年把「山城防禦」由零星建議做成制度，移制置司於重慶、依山築城、以鹽井之利養兵，使蒙古初年南下時沒有立刻拿到可用的攻城辦法；但他1253年病卒，接任的趙覺（趙與時）主持的防線在1256年前後已被突破。守將之中，重慶的王堅與釣魚城的張珏最為有名：1259年蒙哥汗兵臨重慶、釣魚城，兩城的抵抗使蒙古第一次攻宋的總攻停了下來，張珏守到1276年被擒，直到1279年南宋覆亡之際釣魚城才最後易手。蒙古一方，蒙哥汗自1251年即位起主持南征，1256年下令出兵，1258年親率大軍入川，最終死於釣魚城下的軍中；忽必烈自1253年征大理起積累漢地經驗，此時負責荊湖方向，1259年兵臨鄂州，聞蒙哥死訊即北返，隨後在汗位之爭中勝出，1260年即汗位。真正把蒙古攻勢串起來的，是劉整：原為南宋沿江防務將領，1256年以宋地城防、沿江舟師編制、糧運與賦稅底細為代價降元，獻上「先取襄樊、再圖江南」的方略，並自請為先鋒，負責自雲南至成都一線的兵站與向导。汪德臣以鞏昌路總管身份統西道兵入蜀，1258年攻重慶，1259年死於釣魚城下的砲石；紐璘領東道兵，自甘肅攻成都、嘉定一線；郭侃以輕騎深入宋境至鄂州、潭州一線，其事跡見於《元史·郭侃傳》，數字極為誇張，當作宣傳文字看待為宜；兀良合台則以雲南大將身份在交趾與廣西一線策應。
peopleEn: More names survive on the Mongol side than on the Song side. The decisive figure on the Song side was Yu Jie: in his dozen years in Sichuan he turned hill-fort defence from a scattered proposal into a system, moving the directorate to Chongqing, building towns on the heights, and maintaining troops on the revenue of the salt wells, so that the Mongols on their first descent found no ready method of taking cities. But he died of illness in 1253, and the line defended under his successor Zhao Jue, who was Zhao Yushi, was already being broken through around 1256. Among the defenders, Wang Jian of Chongqing and Zhang Jue of Diaoyu are the best known: when Möngke's army stood before Chongqing and Diaoyu in 1259, the resistance of those two cities stopped the first general offensive the Mongols had launched against Song, and Zhang Jue held out until his capture in 1276, with Diaoyu changing hands only at the very end of the Southern Song in 1279. On the Mongol side, Möngke Khan directed the southern campaign from the time of his accession in 1251, ordered the troops out in 1256, and led the main army into Sichuan in 1258, only to die in the camp below Diaoyu. Kublai had been accumulating experience in Chinese lands since the conquest of Dali in 1253 and was responsible for the Jinghu direction; in 1259 he stood before Ezhou, and the news of Möngke's death sent him back north, after which he won the contest for the khanship and was enthroned in 1260. The figure who really tied the Mongol attack together was Liu Zheng. Formerly a Song officer in charge of the river defences, he defected in 1256, paying for his new service with details of the Song defences, of the organisation of the river fleet, of grain transport and of the fiscal base, and he offered the plan of taking Xiangyang and Fancheng first and the Yangtze valley afterwards. He asked to serve in the van and took charge of the supply stations and the guides on the line from Yunnan to Chengdu. Wang Dechen led the western column into Sichuan as commander of the Gongchang circuit, assaulted Chongqing in 1258 and was killed by stone-thrown ammunition below Diaoyu in 1259. Nülin led the eastern column, advancing from Gansu towards Chengdu and Jiading. Guo Kan took light cavalry deep into Song territory as far as the Ezhou and Tanzhou lines, and his exploits are recorded in the biography of Guo Kan in the History of Yuan, where the figures are grossly inflated and the account is best read as propaganda. Yuanliangtai, the great captain of Yunnan, operated on the Jiaozhi and Guangxi front in support.
kits: 卡面的配重投石車，是蒙古攻城序列的骨幹遠程火力。宋元之間稱之為「砲」，十二世紀的中國城防已大量使用這類長臂配重投射器，蒙古自攻西夏與金地起便把它帶進每一次圍城，1256年之後更把西域回回的砲手與砲架技術編入軍隊，使配重砲在攻城時與雲梯、穴地、撞竿、壕溝配合：先以砲壓制城頭與城樓，破壞女牆、門樓與守軍陣位，再由穴地道插入火藥破門，或以雲梯與懸梯登城。宋軍這邊的投射器與器械同樣齊全：弓弩為射擊群的主體，各式強弩與床弩壓制城頭，霹靂砲與火藥箭對付逼近的攻城雲梯，檑木、滾石、撞竿用於破門與反制攻城塔；守城還靠陷坑、鹿角、拒馬與竹城牆。但器械好壞並非這場戰爭的關鍵，關鍵在地形。配重砲需平地、需距離、需足夠的砲手與拋臂展開的空間，對著依山而建的釣魚城便幾乎無從施展：砲位受限於坡地，抬高之後射程不過數十步，坡下就是守軍的射界與落石區。蒙古在四川真正倚賴的不是砲，而是騎兵的機動、封鎖與工程。裝備的另一半是後勤：蒙古靠馬群自帶乳酪、肉乾與炒米，卻沒有蜀地的鹽、稻與藥材，攻城又需大量木料與石彈，於是遠征裝備與四川糧源之間的矛盾貫穿全役；運輸更受三峽與川江限制，蒙古水軍薄弱，騎兵主力只能走陸路，糧車要繞行山道，進攻節奏因此被拖慢。馬上武器是彎弓、標槍與馬刀，鎧以皮甲札甲為主，入蜀後大量補入降軍裝備，攻城時另用木製攻樓、懸梯、穴地支架與火藥器具。
kitsEn: The counterweight trebuchet shown on the card is the backbone of the Mongol siege train's long-range firepower. Between Song and Yuan it was called a pao, and Chinese city defences of the twelfth century already used this kind of long-armed counterweight projector in quantity; the Mongols carried it into every siege from the campaigns against Western Xia and Jin onward, and after 1256 they folded into their army the Huihui trebuchet crews and the timber frames from the western regions, so that the counterweight engine worked together with scaling ladders, tunnelling, rams and ditches. The trebuchet first pinned the parapet and the towers and broke the wall-walk, the gatehouse and the formations of the defenders; then sappers tunnelled under the wall to place powder and blow the gate, or the ladders and folding hanging ladders were carried up. The Song were no less fully equipped: bows and crossbows made up the mass of the shooting group, heavy crossbows and bed crossbows dominating the wall-walk, thunder-crash bombs and fire arrows clearing the assault ladders that came close to the wall, while logs, boulders and rams were used to break gates and to knock down the attacking towers; on the defensive side they relied on pits, abatis, chevaux-de-frise and bamboo palisades. Yet the quality of the engines was not what decided this war; the terrain was. A counterweight engine needs level ground, needs range, and needs enough crews and enough room to unfold its throwing arm, and against a hill town such as Diaoyu it was very nearly helpless. The emplacement was cramped by the slope, and once raised the range was a matter of a few dozen paces, with the defenders' line of fire and their stone-fall directly below. What the Mongols truly relied on in Sichuan was not the trebuchet but the mobility of their cavalry, their blockade and their engineering. The other half of the equipment was logistics: the Mongols carried their own cheese, dried meat and fried rice on the horses, but they had none of Sichuan's salt, rice or medicinal plants, and a siege required large quantities of timber and stone shot, so the contradiction between the equipment of a steppe expedition and the food of Sichuan ran through the whole campaign. Transport was further constrained by the gorges and the upper Yangtze: the Mongol river force was weak, the main body of cavalry had to go by land, and the grain wagons had to take the mountain tracks, which slowed the tempo of attack. The arms of the horsemen were the composite bow, the lance and the sabre; armour was chiefly leather and lamellar, replenished after the entry into Sichuan with the equipment of surrendered troops, and the siege train added timber assault towers, folding ladders, the shoring for tunnelling, and powder devices.
tactics: 蒙古在四川的戰術，一開始是分進合擊。1256年之後，蒙古計畫以多路大軍同時壓入宋境：自甘肅沿沔州、階州入蜀的一路取成都，自雲南北上的一路策應荊湖與廣西，主力自河套南下，三路互相策應，使宋廷無法集中兵力對付任何一路；其核心手法仍是蒙古的老辦法——圍城打援，以一部兵力抵住城下的宋軍主力，另一部切斷其外援與糧道，迫守軍在饑疲中自行崩解。進攻城牆時，蒙古把砲、穴地與雲梯編成一體：砲先打掉城樓與女牆，穴地兵在牆根下掘進，木板與支柱不斷加固，最後以火藥爆破或撞門而入；攻城塔與懸梯則用於在砲火掩護下貼近城頭。與此同時，蒙古的騎兵在川西平原上展開封鎖，斷絕沿江鹽、糧的運輸，並不斷打擊宋廷從湖廣北上的一批批援軍，試圖在山城之外先把宋廷的戰爭機器掐斷。宋方的戰術建立在餘玠留下的山城體系上：把重慶、合州、嘉定等城移到山上，進可控制江面與鹽井，退可依險固守，糧食靠山田梯田與井鹽收入自給，儘量避免在平原上與蒙古騎兵決戰；各山城之間互為犄角，援軍沿江逆流北上，必要時以火藥箭與霹靂砲清除城下的攻城器械。1256年之後，蒙古在蜀中的最大困難不是攻城不破，而是攻不下：蜀道艱險、糧道綿長、牛馬在山道與瘴癘中大量減損，進攻的節奏被迫放慢，於是整場戰役從速決的攻城戰，拖成漫長的封鎖與消耗。
tacticsEn: The Mongol method in Sichuan began as a convergence of separate columns. After 1256 the plan was to press into Song territory at the same time from several directions: one army entering Sichuan from Gansu along Mianzhou and Jiezhou to take Chengdu, one coming north out of Yunnan to support Jinghu and Guangxi, and the main body descending from the Ordos, the three covering one another so that the Song court could never concentrate its forces against any one of them. The core method remained the old Mongol one: to besiege one point in order to draw another, holding the Song main force before the city with one part of the army while another severed its reinforcements and its supply road, so that the garrison would collapse of hunger and exhaustion. In the assault on the wall the Mongols welded trebuchet, tunnelling and ladders into a single sequence: the engines first knocked down the towers and the wall-walk, sappers drove their gallery in at the foot of the wall, plank and prop were added as they advanced, and the gate was finally burst with powder or forced with a ram; assault towers and folding hanging ladders were brought in under cover of the artillery to close with the wallhead. At the same time the Mongol cavalry spread out across the western Sichuan plain, cutting the salt and grain carried along the river and striking the successive columns of Song reinforcements coming north from Huguang, in the attempt to strangle the Song war machine outside the hill towns altogether. The Song tactics rested on the system of hill forts left behind by Yu Jie: Chongqing, Hezhou, Jiading and the other seats were moved up the mountain, able to control the river and the salt wells in advance and to fall back on their defences in retreat, provisioned by terraced fields and the revenue of the salt wells, and avoiding pitched battle with Mongol cavalry on the plain as far as possible. The forts covered one another, relief forces moved up the river against the current, and fire arrows and thunder-crash bombs were used to clear the engines working at the foot of the walls. After 1256 the greatest difficulty the Mongols faced in Sichuan was not the failure of their siege engines but the simple fact that they could not take the towns: the roads were terrible, the supply lines enormously long, and oxen and horses were lost in large numbers on the mountain tracks and amid the miasma of the region, so the tempo of attack slowed and the whole campaign was turned from a siege meant to be decided quickly into a long blockade and war of attrition.
data: 可以核實的數字不多，但有幾項相當硬。時間線是：1251年蒙哥汗即位，1253年忽必烈平大理，1256年蒙古正式大舉攻宋、劉整降元，1258年蒙哥親率主力入川，1259年二月開始攻合州釣魚城，蒙哥汗在是年夏初死於軍中，同年忽必烈兵臨鄂州，賈似道在私下議和。此後南宋又撐了近二十年：釣魚城守到1276年守將張珏被擒，1279年南宋在崖山覆亡時釣魚城最後易手；蒙古自1253年滅大理到1279年滅宋，前後二十六年。距離方面，雲南大理到成都約一千公里，蒙古自河套到成都逾二千公里，合州釣魚城距成都約四百公里，這幾個數字說明蒙古在蜀中的補給線何等長。攻城時間：1259年蒙古自二月起攻釣魚城，屢攻不下，直至同年夏蒙哥死而解圍，這是蒙古第一次在宋人面前長期受挫的攻城。兵力方面，各史多作「十餘萬」乃至「數十萬」之說，這類概數只能當作量級看待，實際列陣的戰兵遠少於此；《元史·郭侃傳》記郭侃以數百騎深入宋境、行程七百餘里、斬獲以萬計，同樣是明顯誇張的宣傳性記載，不宜當作實數。石彈重量與射程方面，十二世紀配重砲所發的石彈從數十斤到百餘斤不等，射程常以數百步計，這是當時器械的通例，而非此役的專門記載。可以確定的損失是消耗而非數字：蜀道與氣候造成蒙古軍中疫病流行，牛馬大量減損，這正是蒙哥死後蒙古一度全軍北撤的原因之一。
dataEn: There are not many figures that can be verified, but a few are hard. The chronology runs: Möngke Khan took the throne in 1251; Kublai reduced Dali in 1253; the Mongols launched their great offensive against Song and Liu Zheng defected in 1256; Möngke led the main army into Sichuan in 1258; the siege of Diaoyu at Hezhou began in the second month of 1259, and Möngke died in the camp in the early summer of that year, while in the same season Kublai stood before Ezhou and Jia Sidao came to terms in private. The Song then held on for nearly twenty more years: Diaoyu was defended until 1276, when its commander Zhang Jue was taken, and the town changed hands only at the end of the Song at Yaoshan in 1279; from the reduction of Dali in 1253 to the fall of the Song in 1279 the Mongols needed twenty-six years. As to distances: from Dali in Yunnan to Chengdu is about a thousand kilometres, from the Ordos to Chengdu more than two thousand, and from Diaoyu at Hezhou to Chengdu about four hundred, which gives some measure of how long the Mongol supply line in Sichuan was. On the duration of the siege: the Mongols attacked Diaoyu from the second month of 1259 and did not take it, the siege lasting until Möngke's death in the summer of that year brought it to an end; this was the first siege in which the Mongols were long checked by the Song. As for numbers of men, the histories speak commonly of a hundred thousand or tens of thousands more; such round figures can only be read as orders of magnitude, the actual battle lines being far smaller. The biography of Guo Kan in the History of Yuan records that he entered Song territory with several hundred cavalry, covered more than seven hundred li and took prisoners and kills by the tens of thousands; this is equally inflated and belongs to the language of propaganda rather than to the record of fact. As for the weight and range of the stones, the stones thrown by twelfth-century counterweight engines ran from several tens of jin to more than a hundred, and the range was commonly reckoned in several hundred paces; that is the general practice of the engines of the age rather than a specific record of this campaign. What can be established is consumption rather than a number: the roads and the climate brought disease into the Mongol camp and destroyed great numbers of oxen and horses, which is one of the reasons the Mongols withdrew north after Möngke's death.
cause: 打起嚟有四層緣由。最外一層是蒙古的既定方針：成吉思汗臨終留下滅金、滅宋的遺命，1251年即位的蒙哥汗接下這件事，1253年先取大理，就是為了打開南面的通道。往裡一層是雲南與四川的資源與通道：大理境內的馬群與滇池一帶的糧食是蒙古遠征的支柱，而南宋為遏制大理，也曾在蒙古西征之際出兵西南；雲南既已歸順，蒙古自然要把川滇連成一條完整的西路，順帶把南宋在西部的支撐點切斷。再往裡是劉整。1256年他以宋地沿江城防、舟師編制、軍糧轉運與賦稅底細為代價降元，帶來的是蒙古此前最缺的東西：情報；他獻上的方略是取襄樊以為根本，先斷兩淮與荊湖的聯絡，再圖江南，而四川正是襄樊西面的屏障與糧源。最深的一層在蒙古內部：忽必烈與阿里不哥爭奪汗位，1256年後忽必烈以經略漢地、經營雲南與南征宋境來積累自己的勢力與財富，攻宋因此既是國策，也是爭位的手段。而宋廷這邊的回應是硬拒：不接受稱臣與納貢的條件，不放還來使；餘玠之後的四川防線被史家批評為守禦失當，沿江諸州各自為守，糧餉調度又屢屢受制於荊湖。1256年夏，四層因素疊在一起，蒙古的兵鋒便同時壓向成都府路與荊湖。
causeEn: There were four layers of reason for the fighting. The outermost was the settled Mongol policy: Genghis Khan left behind the task of destroying Jin and Song, Möngke Khan took it up on his accession in 1251, and the reduction of Dali in 1253 was done precisely to open the road to the south. A layer deeper was the wealth and the lines of communication of Yunnan and Sichuan: the horse herds of Dali and the grain of the Dianchi basin had been the prop of the Mongol expeditions, and the Song, seeking to hold Dali in check, had also sent troops into the southwest while the Mongols were campaigning in the west; with Yunnan now submitted, the Mongols naturally needed to join Yunnan and Sichuan into one continuous western route, and at the same time to cut the Song off at its western pillar. Deeper still was Liu Zheng. In 1256 he defected, paying for his new service with the river defences of the Song, the organisation of its fleet, the movement of its military grain and the details of its fiscal base, and what he brought the Mongols was the one thing they had most lacked: information. The plan he proposed was to make Xiangyang and Fancheng the base, to sever the connection between Lianghuai and Jinghu first, and to take the Yangtze valley afterwards, and Sichuan was precisely the screen and the granary on the western side of Xiangyang. The deepest layer lay inside the Mongol empire: Kublai and his brother Arig Qesh were contending for the khanship, and after 1256 Kublai used the administration of Chinese lands, the holding of Yunnan and the war in Song territory to build up his own position and revenue, so that the attack on Song was at once a matter of state policy and a bid for power. The Song court's answer was a hard refusal: it would not accept the terms of submission and tribute and would not release the envoys; the Sichuan line after Yu Jie was faulted by the historians for its faulty defence, the river prefectures each defended themselves alone, and the movement of grain was repeatedly at the mercy of Jinghu. When the four layers came together in the summer of 1256, the Mongol spearhead pressed against the Chengdu circuit and against Jinghu at the same time.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果遠遠溢出四川。1259年蒙哥汗死於釣魚城下，直接改變了歐亞的局勢：正在西征的蒙古遠征軍因大汗之死中止進攻，歐洲與拜占庭因此多出數十年的喘息，而蒙古帝國隨即分裂成四大汗國，東亞的元朝走上獨立一途。就宋元而言，此役之後蒙古改變了戰法：不再以速決攻城為唯一目標，而是把「先取襄樊、再順江而下」作為全局，以工程、封鎖與長期消耗配合。技術與人員的流動同樣可觀：劉整、郭侃一類漢人將領進入蒙古的指揮系統，蒙古的火藥攻城器（震天雷、火砲）與配重砲在此役之後不斷成熟，而配重砲的技術也隨蒙古進入西亞，稍後又由十字軍方面傳回歐洲，十四世紀歐洲的攻城戰裡出現了同類器械。四川本身則被改造成元朝西南的根據地：平川州郡提供稻米、井鹽與布帛，成為元代財賦的重要來源，驛路也自雲南與甘肅一路修通成都，為日後進攻荊湖與襄樊輸送兵馬與糧食。南宋這邊，山城防禦的效力得到證明，釣魚城一守二十年，成為後世講述「以山城拒蒙」的標本；宋廷卻也因此更加倚賴荊湖與兩淮，把主力調去荊襄，1270年代襄陽陷落後，元軍順江而下，1276年臨安出降，1279年崖山之戰後南宋覆亡，釣魚城同年最後易手。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached far beyond Sichuan. The death of Möngke below Diaoyu in 1259 changed the situation of Eurasia directly: the Mongol armies campaigning in the west halted their advance on the news of the Great Khan's death, and Europe and Byzantium gained decades of breathing room, while the Mongol empire split into the four khanates and the Yuan in the Far East went on its own way. For Song and Yuan alike, the campaign changed Mongol methods: no longer was the rapid reduction of cities the only object, and the strategy of taking Xiangyang and Fancheng first and then coming down the river became the whole design, with engineering, blockade and long attritional wear applied to it. The movement of skills and men was equally remarkable: Chinese commanders such as Liu Zheng and Guo Kan entered the Mongol command structure, the Mongol powder siege engines, the thunder-crash bomb and the bombard, and the counterweight trebuchet went on maturing after this campaign, and the trebuchet's technique travelled with the Mongols into West Asia and was later carried back towards Europe by the crusading side, so that the same class of engine appears in European siege warfare of the fourteenth century. Sichuan itself was turned into the southwestern base of the Yuan: the prefectures of the plain supplied rice, salt from the wells and cloth and silk, and became an important source of Yuan revenue, while the post road was carried through from Yunnan and Gansu to Chengdu, moving troops and grain for the later campaigns against Jinghu and Xiangyang. On the Song side the effect of the hill-fort system was demonstrated: Diaoyu held for twenty years and became the standard example of later accounts of resistance to the Mongols from a hill town. Yet the Song court also grew more dependent than ever on Jinghu and Lianghuai, moving its main strength towards Jingxiang; after Xiangyang fell in the 1270s the Yuan army came down the river, Lin'an surrendered in 1276, the Song was destroyed after the battle of Yaoshan in 1279, and Diaoyu changed hands in the same year.
result: 結果是雙方各得一半，蒙古先勝後敗。1256年之後，蒙古在四川陸續攻下成都、嘉定、潼川等川西與沔州的州府，取得平原上的稻田、井鹽與驛道，也取得一支可供南征的四川降軍與糧源；然而餘玠留下的山城一個接一個頂住了蒙古的砲火，合州釣魚城尤其，1259年蒙古自二月圍攻至夏初，屢攻不下，最終不是被攻破，而是因蒙哥汗死於軍中而中止。蒙哥之死使蒙古第一次大規模攻宋的總攻功虧一簣：忽必烈自鄂州撤兵北返，荊湖方向的戰役也一併收束，蒙古內部的汗位之爭隨即開打，南宋則在賈似道主持下取得為期十餘年的喘空間，直到1260年代末蒙古再攻襄陽才重新開打。從器械的角度看，這場戰役同時給出兩個結論：配重投石車這類大型攻城器在平原上確實有效，卻不是無所不能，它在依山築起的山城面前幾乎無處施展；而決定勝負的，是攻城器之外的東西——糧道長度、騎兵封鎖、山城裡的屯田與自給，以及一位大汗的性命。蒙古直到1279年才在崖山真正滅掉南宋，比多數人預想的多了二十多年。
resultEn: The result was a share each for both sides, with the Mongols winning first and losing later. After 1256 the Mongols took one after another the prefectures of western Sichuan and of Mianzhou — Chengdu, Jiading, Tongchuan among them — gaining the rice fields, the salt wells and the post road of the plain, and also a Sichuan army of surrendered troops and a supply of grain for the campaign south. But the hill towns left by Yu Jie held off the Mongol artillery one after another, and Diaoyu at Hezhou above all: in 1259 the Mongols besieged it from the second month to the early summer, never took it, and the siege was not ended by a breach but by the death of Möngke Khan in the camp. The death of Möngke wrecked the first general offensive the Mongols had launched against the Song: Kublai withdrew from before Ezhou and went north, the campaign in the Jinghu direction was closed down with it, and the contest for the khanship opened inside the Mongol empire at once, while the Song bought itself more than ten years of breathing space under Jia Sidao and did not have to fight again until the Mongols returned to Xiangyang in the late 1260s. From the point of view of the engines, the campaign gave two conclusions at once. A large siege engine such as the counterweight trebuchet was indeed effective on the plain, but it was not omnipotent: against a hill town it had almost nowhere to stand. And what decided the outcome lay outside the engines altogether — the length of the supply road, the blockade by cavalry, the terraced fields and self-provisioning inside the hill towns, and the life of a single Great Khan. The Mongols did not truly destroy the Southern Song until Yaoshan in 1279, more than twenty years beyond what most had expected.
